model.rationale: This Manhattan-based seat's D+33 fundamentals make it one of the most Democratic districts in the country, and Lasher's dominant fundraising and heavy outside backing leave Republican Caroline Shinkle with no visible path. Markets agree, pricing the Democrat near 98%, so the forecast stays at a large Democratic margin with modest uncertainty.
model.watch: Any sign of significant Republican outside spending or a polling surprise would be needed to move this race toward competitiveness.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Jerry Nadler (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
NY-12, covering Manhattan's Upper West and East Sides, is among the most Democratic districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+33. Jerry Nadler's retirement created an open seat, but the Democratic nominee Micah Lasher enters the general election with overwhelming advantages: he has raised $3.3 million and drawn more than $10 million in outside support, while Republican Caroline Shinkle has raised about $155,000 with no reported outside spending.

Prediction markets price the Democratic candidate at roughly 98% to win, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. Two independent candidates on the ballot raise minimal funds and are unlikely to affect the outcome. The forecast expects a comfortable Democratic hold in the low-thirty-point range, with the main uncertainty being turnout in a low-profile open-seat contest.
